title: Latency-aware merge-batcher with KV zoning and GPU memory safeguards
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal:
Tune the continuous batching scheduler to better handle mixed workload profiles (short prompts + long responses) by merging compatible slots without causing KV cache churn or GPU OOMs. The feature introduces a latency-aware merge window and a KV 'zoning' concept that protects hot prefixes and prioritizes eviction candidates by age/priority. We also add lightweight GPU memory safeguards (watermarks + pinned spill) to avoid tail OOMs when coalescing high token-cost responses.

Background / Motivation:
- In production we see a recurring pattern: a high volume of short inference requests (single-turn prompts) interleaved with infrequent, long-response decoding requests.
- The current continuous batcher aggressively coalesces by time window and sequence length buckets which sometimes causes: KV cache thrash (evicting active prefixes), GPU memory fragmentation, and 99th-pct latency spikes during large merges.
- Prior tickets addressed various batching heuristics (length-priority bins, slot segmentation) but none introduce a merged policy that coordinates KV protection and GPU-level watermarks.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Merge window + stride-awareness: introduce a stride-aware merge window that prefers coalescing shorter prompts with queued decoders only if the resulting token budget for a slot is below a dynamic per-GPU merge threshold. Stride-awareness means the scheduler inspects the expected decode trajectory rather than just current length.

2) KV zoning: partition the KV cache logically into three zones: HOT (protected prefixes with recent hits), WARM (candidate for eviction but with some grace), and COLD (evict-first). When merging, the scheduler computes the merged request's KV footprint and avoids merges that would force HOT -> COLD eviction. Zones defined by time-since-last-hit and request priority.

3) GPU memory safeguards: maintain soft/hard watermarks per-GPU for KV + activation memory. If a merge would cross the soft watermark, scheduler will either: a) delay merge and favor preemption for shorter tasks, b) spill cold KV segments to pinned host memory (best-effort), or c) throttle merge window. Hard watermark disallows merge and signals fallback to smaller model variant or queued execution.

4) Token-budget-based slot assignment: each slot has a token budget quota. Merges are permitted only when combined estimated tokens <= slot quota. Quotas adapt to observed average sequence length and can be tuned per-deployment class (hosted vs dedicated).

5) Telemetry and rollout: add metrics for KV hit-rate by zone, merge-induced eviction events, per-GPU soft/hard watermark breaching, and per-merge latency delta. Instrument synthetic mixed workloads and a small A/B cohort in dedicated capacity.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- Under mixed workload (70% short prompts < 16 tokens, 30% long decodes > 512 tokens): 95th-pct latency reduced by >= 7% compared to baseline scheduler for the same throughput.
- KV hit-rate for HOT zone remains >= 98% (no regressions).
- OOM incidents due to merging reduced by >= 90% on canary hosts.
- No more than 5% regression in p50 latency across neutral workloads.
- End-to-end test coverage for merge policy decision and KV zoning logic in unit/integration harness.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): microbenchmark merge heuristics in the local scheduler simulator. Produce simple model of KV footprint estimation and GPU watermarks.
- Phase 2 (prototype, 2 weeks): implement scheduler hooks: stride estimator, merge-eligibility function, KV zoning metadata updates, and soft/hard watermark checks. Add feature flags.
- Phase 3 (canary, 2-3 weeks): enable on a small subset of Dedicated nodes and run synthetic mixed workloads + customer shadowing. Collect metrics and iterate thresholds.
- Phase 4 (rollout): staged rollout to Hosted (first lower-tier regions), then to Dedicated with opt-in.

Telemetry & Dashboards to add:
- merge_attempts_total (labels: gpu_id, merged=true/false, reason)
- kv_zone_hit_rate{zone=HOT/WARM/COLD}
- kv_evictions_by_zone
- gpu_watermark_events{soft/hard}
- merge_latency_delta (comparison of merged vs non-merged avg latency)
- merge_related_oom_count

Fallbacks / rollbacks:
- Feature flag to disable merge-batcher and revert to previous continuous batching policy.
- Auto-fallback: if per-host OOM rate crosses threshold in canary, automatically disable merge decisions on that host.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Cost vs latency: protecting HOT KV prefixes reduces eviction but may increase memory pressure; need to tune watermarks carefully.
- Complexity vs observability: KV zoning adds metadata overhead. We'll minimize by encoding zone bits in existing KV index structure.
- Cross-GPU merges: for sharded models merging across GPUs has more complex eviction implications — start with single-GPU-safe merges only.

Acceptance test harness and benchmarks:
- Extend the existing scheduler simulator (bench/scheduler_sim) with workload generator for mixed prompt/response distributions.
- Add CI perf job that runs regression for key percentiles on a small config.

Dependencies:
- ENG-67214 (adaptive-stride-prefetch-kv-shard-orchestration)
- ENG-22111 (length-aware-kv-cache-batcher-optimizer)

Deliverables:
- Scheduler change with feature flag that implements merge policy + KV zoning
- Unit tests, integration tests, and perf benchmarks
- Dashboards and alerting for new telemetry signals
- PRD link to rollout plan and canary criteria
comments: 2026-02-11 Priya Patel: Kicked off spike. Built a simple simulator that models token budgets and KV footprint for merged requests. Initial sims show potential 10% tail improvement if we prevent HOT-prefix eviction.
2026-02-16 Liam Chen: Reviewed spike results. Agreed on stride-aware merge window. Asked for explicit test for worst-case that previously caused OOM on xenon-2 cluster.

2026-02-23 Engineering Sync (Liam Chen): Prototype branch created at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4125. Primary hooks live in pkg/scheduler/merge_policy.go and kv/zone_manager.go. Please don't merge until unit tests are green.

2026-03-03 Automated Bench: ran synthetic mixed workload against prototype on canary nodes. KV HOT hit-rate remained 99.1%, soft-watermark events 12% lower than baseline, but observed 2 regressions in p50 on small hosts when quotas were conservatively low.

2026-03-08 Design Review (Aisha Raman): Suggested adding per-customer merge policies (customer-level opt-out) and adding a simple cost model to prefer merges that reduce overall token compute, not just latency.
2026-03-10 PR Feedback (Ben Morales): Unit tests failing under race conditions for zone updates; added locking around per-slot metadata. Also requested a flag to disable pinned spill for tests.
2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Updated thresholds after bench runs. Preparing canary rollout for 20 dedicated hosts next week. Created canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/merge-batcher-canary
